_comment: klt erc supply spec for the sampler_core composed GDS -- the T1
item-11 (power delivery, structural) supply read for this block
(issue #154), mirroring gf180-drone-fc's layout/digital/
erc-supply-spec.json worked example.
Run it against the composed, DRC- and LVS-clean cell:
klt erc layout/sampler_core/sampler_core.gds \
layout/sampler_core/erc-supply-spec.json --format json
What this spec asserts, and why each piece is shaped this way:
- Layer/datatype numbers are sky130's own, resolved from the PDK's
`libs.tech/klayout/tech/sky130A.lyp` (open_pdks
c6d73a35f524070e85faff4a6a9eef49553ebc2b, layout/pdk.json's
pin) and cross-checked against klayout-tools' curated sky130
deck layer table (decks/sky130.py: diff.drawing 65/20,
tap.drawing 65/44, poly.drawing 66/20, li1.drawing 67/20,
mcon.drawing 67/44, met1.drawing 68/20, via 68/44,
met2.drawing 69/20). No number here is carried over from
another PDK's spec.
- `stackup` is the fabrication order from the gate layer up
through every routing level this block actually uses.
`klt layers layout/sampler_core/sampler_core.gds` shows the
stream's top metal is met2 (69/20); no met3/met4/met5 shapes
exist, so the stack stops at met2 -- declaring empty levels
would add zero geometry and zero evidence.
- stackup[0] `poly` (66/20, poly.drawing) carries `role: gate`
-- klt erc's own contract requires the gate-poly layer first,
in fabrication order. It also sets `active_layer` to the
diffusion layer `diff.drawing` (65/20), so gate area -- and
hence each antenna-ratio denominator -- is `poly n diff`
instead of raw poly area (klayout-tools #1979/#2001): this
block's ring stages route real poly interconnect between
stages, and raw-poly area would count that interconnect as
gate oxide area it does not have. NOTE: `active_layer` is
honored by klt builds at/after #2001
(cfec44c119b60227ba3593cbb3293029f74e4165); the pinned
released build (layout/pdk.json ci_klt_install == 0.5.0,
the newest PyPI tag) predates it and would silently ignore
this key -- the committed report (erc.json) was therefore
generated with a post-#2001 dev build pinned by full commit
SHA, the same documented-exception workaround
layout/sampler_dff/README.md already uses for legs[]
(klayout-tools #1529/#1536). See that README section for
the exact venv recipe; erc.json's own provenance records
the build that actually ran.
- stackup[1] `li1` (67/20, li1.drawing) with label_layer 67/5
(li1.label): li1 is this block's local interconnect AND the
layer the leaf cells draw their supply pin text on -- the
67/5 stream carries `vdd`/`vss` pin labels, the per-cell
`*_vdd`/`*_vss` rail labels, the ring-local `vddr` rail
labels, and the array's `nwell_vdd` well-tie pad labels.
- stackup[2] `met1` (68/20, met1.drawing) with label_layer
68/5 (met1.label): met1 carries the block's promoted supply
pin text -- the `vddr1`..`vddr4` per-ring pin labels
(one each, promoted bare pins by ro_array_core's place
stage) plus `vdd`/`vss` rail and strap text
- stackup[3] `met2` (69/20, met2.drawing) with label_layer
69/5 (met2.label): the top level, carrying its own `vdd`/
`vss`/`vddr` rail text. Labels on a stackup level whose
label_layer is not declared are simply invisible to this
read; all three label layers here actually carry supply
text in the stream, so all three are declared.
- `vias[]` bridges the stackup roles with sky130's own cut
layers, per the curated deck table: licon1 (66/44,
licon1.drawing) joins poly-role geometry to li1;
mcon (67/44, mcon.drawing) joins li1 to met1; the
met1-to-met2 cut (68/44, `via.drawing`) joins met1 to
met2. licon1 physically also lands on diff and tap
regions (that is how wells and substrate are contacted);
diffusion/tap are deliberately NOT stackup conductors
here, so that path is out of this model's scope -- see
the README section: the device-aware well/tie coverage
is exactly the `erc.missing_tie` half this run does not
compute, not an oversight.
- `nets[]`: every supply the block's own netlist declares.
design/sampler_core.spice's `.subckt sampler_core` pins are
`vddr1 vddr2 vddr3 vddr4 vdd vss` -- six supplies, all
declared `kind: supply` so a short between any two reads
as `erc.supply_short` rather than the general
`erc.multiply_driven_net`, and each must resolve to exactly
ONE electrical island (no `erc.unconnected_net` naming it
-- that rule fires on zero matches AND on more than one).
The four `vddrN` names, not the bare `vddr`: the
ring-local text label `vddr` (and the per-stage strap
names `g_vddr_m1`/`s1..s4_vddr_m1`) repeat inside EVERY
ring, so declaring `vddr` as one supply resolves to four
disconnected islands -- one per ring rail -- which is the
netlist's own topology, not a defect: `ro_array_core`
routes each ring's supply as its own rail and promotes
`vddr1`-`vddr4` as four separate block pins
(layout/ro_array_core/README.md: 'the four vddr rails
... stay separate, exactly as intended'), and
layout/sampler_core/lvs.json's `net_correspondence`
carries all four as separate reference-side nets. The
block-level supply names are therefore the per-pin
`vddr1..vddr4`, exactly as the netlist declares them.
(`vdd` and `vss` each resolve to a single island -- the
inter-block strap increments #112/#113 closed both halves
of `vdd`, and `vss` was metal-continuous once its own
four-stage strap landed. The committed erc.json is the
recorded verdict: zero `erc.unconnected_net`, zero
`erc.supply_short`.)
- There is deliberately NO `ties[]` section here, and that
is a recorded gap rather than an oversight (the same
decision, with the same evidence, as gf180-drone-fc's
FRICTION F-034 on the gf180mcu routed digital flow):
klayout-tools#2169 documents that on the pinned RELEASED
klt (0.5.0, which layout/pdk.json's ci_klt_install names
for CI) a `ties[]` entry joins its well/tap regions into
the single unified connectivity graph before extraction,
so a blanket well region shorts every conductor drawn
above it and collapses a routed design into one island
with a FALSE `erc.supply_short` (F-034's four-case
truth table reproduces this exactly; gates[] collapses
from 95 to 1 on the gf180 design). Per klt erc's own
contract, omitting `ties[]` means `erc.missing_tie` is NOT
COMPUTED -- the zero absent from the committed report is
an absence of evidence, not evidence of absence. The
committed erc.json's `erc_coverage` block records this
mechanically on builds that carry it.
The well-tie evidence that stands in for the un-computed
`erc.missing_tie` verdict (all committed-artifact-backed):
1. layout/sampler_core/lvs.json -- `status: match`,
152/152 nets and 264/264 devices, against a SPICE
reference whose every device carries explicit bulk
connections to the supply nets (pfet bulk = the rail
that powers the cell, nfet bulk = vss). The
device-aware extraction models the well/tap path --
an untied well would surface as a floating bulk net
and a topology mismatch, not a match. All four
`VDDR*` supplies plus `VDD` and `VSS` appear in the
`net_correspondence` paired to reference-side nets,
so the supplies were part of the compare (item 11's
analog-column LVS requirement).
2. The same lvs.json VDD correspondence row's
layout-side alias set includes `nwell_vdd` -- the
well-tie pd labels drawn on the nwell tap pads.
3. The merged GDS draws a dedicated `tap.drawing`
(65/44) layer -- 177 shapes, `klt layers
layout/sampler_core/sampler_core.gds` -- the PDK's
own tub-contact marker layer, landed on by licon1
cuts and covered by the supply rails' li1 pads.
This is the geometry `erc.missing_tie` would grade
if the pinned released klt could grade it safely.
